prerequisites: Mathematical Foundations of Robotics and Image Processing

learning_outcomes.text: Apply mathematical design tools of control engineering for robotics.
Select suitable sensors and actuators for robotic systems.
Design and implement path control for robotic systems.
Design and implement basic autonomous capabilities for motion planning, image-based control, and force-torque control.

syllabus_topics: State-space description (representation, solution in time and frequency domain, normal forms)
Digital control systems (z-transform, representation in time and frequency domain, stability, control algorithms)
Structure of industrial motion control systems (cascade control, pre-filters, vibration suppression)
Mathematical methods and description of robotic systems (introduction to kinematics and dynamics of robotic systems)
Motion planning, with focus on global path planning (search and sample-based methods) and trajectory planning in Joint Space and Task Space
Visual Servoing (Image-based Visual Servoing and Position-based Visual Servoing)
Force and torque control with focus on indirect force-torque control using impedance or admittance approach
Implementation of basic algorithms in accompanying exercises
Sensors for position control of robotic systems
Structure of digital motor controls with current and position control
Real-time firmware for digital motor controls with PWM-based power stages
Control methods for DC, Stepper, and BLDC motors
